title: Graphing a Right-Shifted Inverse-Square Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1 / (x - 1)^2 by identifying its parent function, shift, asymptotes, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Horizontal Shift
steps.explanation: Start with the volcano-shaped parent curve y = 1/x^2 and replace x with x - 1 to shift the graph 1 unit to the right.
steps.why: Replacing x with x - 1 translates the graph horizontally right by 1 unit.

steps.title: Determine the Asymptotes, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The vertical asymptote moves to x = 1, the horizontal asymptote remains y = 0, and because (x - 1)^2 > 0 for all x != 1, the range is (0, infinity).
steps.why: A positive numerator divided by a positive square yields strictly positive outputs.

steps.title: Find the y-Intercept and Symmetric Points
steps.explanation: Both branches rise toward +infinity along the vertical line of symmetry x = 1, passing symmetrically through (0, 1) and (2, 1), with no x-intercepts.
steps.why: The graph is symmetric about the vertical asymptote x = 1.
